items.title: Manny Gabriel Interview, 1965-07-27
items.q: I know Billy Goodson was her name, I guess.

ctx.x: Yeah, it was around the corner of the hoist band with Louis Deming. So, I said, now I'm going to get a saxophone. So, Joe heard about us. Joe said, Joe said, came to the house. He said, man, do you want a saxophone? I heard. I said, yeah, but I ain't got the money to buy nothing. He said, you come up to the house tomorrow and bring any kind of money you want to bring. I'll get your saxophone if you worry about that. So, I went up there and the boy Larry, Larry, he had a saxophone because he must have failed on…
I know Billy Goodson was her name, I guess. From Pensacola. Sadie? What was the name? I don't know. That's Ken. Didi. Didi's wife.

Didi's wife's sister. She was our fan. I played Sadie. This fella played banjo. I'll get his name. He stood up to town. I'll call his name after a while. My buddy was on the trumpet and I was on the clarinet trying to be on the drum. I can't call his name either. Sanji. Sanji. I don't know if his French name was Sanji. He played the guitar. You'll ask somebody else about him. They'll tell you about Sanji. He played banjo. He spoke a whole lot of Creole. He was bigger than you and he was a bunch of light-skinned.…
